## TL;DR

I addressed the three review findings on the existing task branch. Reaper eligibility now follows the actual 25-minute run cap because a validation container is created only after its host slot has been acquired. The final removal command no longer treats a lock directory under one SSH user's home as authoritative for all users on the runner. The Runners tab now displays the condition for both a run currently being killed and a historical hung run. The required changed-path check passed, including the full local fallback after all configured runner links failed their probes on the final attempt.

## Work and rationale

The review identified a timing mismatch in the periodic container reaper. The code treated the full host-lock wait plus run timeout as a container's legitimate lifetime, then added a further safety margin. That produced a 45-minute threshold. Inspection of the execution order confirms that the run waits for and acquires its slot before creating the container, so the lock-wait allowance cannot contribute to container age. I changed the reaper's run cap to `REMOTE_RUN_TIMEOUT_MS` (25 minutes), use that same cap when selecting and rechecking candidates, and updated the operator log to state 25 minutes. The five-minute interval remains a quiet-log check, rather than additional age added to eligibility.

The prior final deletion guard serialized through `$HOME/.repoos-validate-locks`. That path is private to the SSH user, so it cannot reliably reveal a validation owned by another account. I removed that home-scoped lock check from the final command. The reaper still excludes locally tracked live names and checks the container's exact name, state, age and recent output before removal. This uses the run timeout and Docker's own state instead of making a cross-user ownership claim from a user-specific directory. The documentation now explains why the 15-minute pre-container wait is excluded and what activity window remains in force.

The backend had recorded a useful `detail`, but the Runners panel omitted it in both places where operators need it. I added a short `hungDetail` to the live active-run status and fill it with the plain condition label while the kill is underway. The historic Hung runs row already receives detailed text from the backend; it now renders that detail too. The panel test covers the live “host idle” cause and historical “output stream was silent” cause.

I also updated the reaper tests to assert the 25-minute cutoff, ensure the final command no longer relies on a user's lock root, and expect a 25-minute reaper log. The existing capture-before-removal and hang-condition tests remain in place. The task's docs describe the updated cleanup behavior.

## Approaches tried

I first followed the code path from candidate listing through the pre-removal inspect and final Docker removal. That showed the threshold was assembled in more than one place, so I aligned candidate selection, the inspection predicate and the user-facing log to the same run cap. For ownership, retaining the lease and trying to broaden its directory would have required a shared filesystem location with permissions and deployment assumptions not established by this code. I instead relied on the invariant already enforced by the run timeout: a run cannot legitimately own a container at or beyond the container age cap. Recent Docker output and a final exact-name check remain as safeguards.

For the UI issue, the event detail did not need a new event schema or a second reason field in historical storage. The active badge gets a short condition label; the existing historical detail is displayed directly. This preserves the backend's recorded evidence and makes it visible where the review finding requested.

## Challenges and blockers

The first scoped check found a TypeScript error because `hungDetail` had been added to the public status shape but not the pool's internal active-run shape. I added it to that internal type, then reran the gate. The next run completed the remote build and tests but stopped locally on formatting; I ran the repository formatter and restarted the full check.

On the final check, the Mac could not complete throughput probes to thinkpad, bee or mini. The configured remote gate reported each host unavailable and fell back to the local full suite. The local build and all test files passed. No live runner cleanup or device-level behavior was exercised during this session; the relevant reaper and UI behavior is covered by automated tests.

## Key learnings

A lock-wait timeout is part of the validation request lifetime, not the lifetime of a container that does not exist until after the lock is acquired. Reaper age thresholds should be based on the resource's creation point in the lifecycle.

A host-side lock under `$HOME` is useful for coordinating jobs run as that account, but it is not a host-wide ownership registry when multiple SSH users can reach the Docker daemon. The 25-minute hard cap gives the reaper a bounded ownership rule without that false assumption.

Finally, recording a cause in an event is not enough for operator visibility if the Runners tab drops the field. The live and historical displays now expose the reason in plain language.
